title: Zariski locally trivial scheme torsor groupoid
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $G$ be a group scheme over $S$, and let $J$ be an $S$-scheme with left $G$-action. Use the scheme torsor pairs, cartesian equivariant arrows and trivial-torsor construction of [def-sfb-scheme-action-torsor-groupoids]. A torsor pair $(E\to T,u:E\to J)$ is Zariski locally trivial if every point of $T$ belongs to the image of an open immersion $j:U\to T$ with an equivariant morphism $t:G\times_S U\to E$ whose square with the projection $G\times_S U\to U$ and $j$ is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define the Zariski torsor groupoid as the full subcategory on these pairs, with its existing projection to schemes over $S$. The canonical general trivial-torsor atlas uses the construction of [def-sfb-affine-action-quotient-stack]. Every trivial pair is Zariski locally trivial (the whole base is a product chart); this law supplies the proof field of the canonical trivial-torsor map $h_J\to\mathcal P_{\mathrm{Zar}}$, with the existing trivial-torsor arrow maps. For $x:T\to J$, write $P_x$ for this trivial pair as an object of the actual fibre over $T$. The discrete groupoid $h_J$ and the notion of fibred groupoid are those of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].
